newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slips, but fares better than Big Board.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slips, but fares better than Big Board.

text.p: Nasdaq shares slipped further on Thursday, but suffered a less severe beating than the Dow industrials, which sank sharply under interest rate pressures, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index dropped 10.83 points or 0.83 percent to an unofficial close of 1293.30. The Dow industrials shed 160 points in its fifth steepest point loss ever. The Dow closed unofficially at 6879.

"The Nasdaq fared better the Dow. The Nasdaq has been so beaten lately that there were some bargain hunters coming out to pick up some cheap deals. With the blue chips being hit, buyers came shopping in the Nasdaq," one trader said.

Technology stocks, which have been hard hit recently, showed moderate gains. Oracle Corp led the technology winners, gaining 2 to 36-1/8 ahead of its third quarter results, which were released after the market closed. Cisco Systems Inc firmed 1-1/8 to 52, Microsoft Corp added 7/8 to 99-5/8.

Less fortunate was Employee Solutions Inc, which shed 4-1/2 to 15-3/8. The Phoenix-based company postponed the release of its fourth quarter results. Overall, decliners beat gainers 2897 to 1430 on total volume of 564 million shares.
